identity.name: Potassium sorbate
identity.chemical_class: Potassium salt of sorbic acid (unsaturated fatty-acid preservative salt)

function.mechanism: Weak-acid preservative activity that is pH-dependent; antimicrobial efficacy is stronger at lower pH.
common_food_categories: Sliced/cut cheeses and processed cheese products

adi.basis: 2019 EFSA follow-up group ADI for sorbic acid (E200) and potassium sorbate (E202), expressed as sorbic acid

efsa.key_finding: EFSA replaced the earlier temporary ADI and established a group ADI of 11 mg/kg bw/day after evaluating EOGRTS data (BMDL 1,110 mg/kg bw/day).

adi.basis: JECFA group ADI reported as 0-25 mg/kg bw for sorbic acid and calcium/potassium/sodium sorbates (expressed as sorbic acid)

concerns.summary: Animal studies reported altered gut microbiota composition and inflammatory markers after sustained potassium sorbate exposure, with partial recovery after washout.
Recent in vivo and in vitro studies reported reproductive, hepatic, oxidative stress, and apoptosis-related effects, often at experimental doses or in mixture settings.
A large observational cohort reported association between higher intake of several preservatives including potassium sorbate and higher type 2 diabetes incidence, without proving causality.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2015/2019 opinions reported no evidence of genotoxic activity for sorbic acid or potassium sorbate in assessed datasets.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2015 identified child-group exceedance concern under higher scenarios (temporary ADI context), and a 2024 regional exposure study reported P95 exceedance scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory consensus supports permitted use with ADI controls, but child/high-consumer exceedance scenarios and emerging non-human/mechanistic signals justify a cautionary moderate tier rather than limited.
key_factors: EFSA and FDA authorization with explicit ADI/GMP framework
EFSA historical temporary ADI reduction and later revision to 11 mg/kg bw/day
Exposure exceedance risk in some high-consumption subgroups
Recent animal/mechanistic and observational human signals requiring continued monitoring
No IARC classification for potassium sorbate
